The appeal panel held that the Final Occupation Certificate (FOC) date was not the date the building works were completed and did not start the statutory warranty period. Under the contract, “building works” meant works carried out, completed, and handed over to the owners; practical completion allowed only minor omissions or defects that did not prevent reasonable use for the usual purpose. Defect rectification during the defects liability period was distinct from the completed building works.

The appeal panel applied section 3B of the Home Building Act (HB Act) to the residential building work, even though the parties’ contract was made in 2009. Section 3B was introduced by the Home Building Amendment Act 2011, effective 1 February 2012; Schedule 4 clause 106(a) stated that the amendments were for the purpose of avoiding doubt and extended them to work commenced or completed before that date.

Under section 3B(1) of the Home Building Act, residential building work is complete on the date it is complete within the meaning of the contract. Section 3B(2) provides that if the contract does not specify when work is complete, completion occurs at practical completion. Section 3B(3) creates a rebuttable presumption of practical completion based on the earliest of specified dates, including handover of possession, the contractor’s last site attendance for relevant work, or issue of an occupation certificate, unless an earlier practical-completion date is established.

The contract did not make provision of an FOC a condition of practical completion. The appeal panel concluded that the Tribunal erred in treating 20 October 2010, the date the FOC was issued, as the completion date. It substituted a finding that completion occurred at practical completion under the contract; the panel said this was 8 July 2010, or, if not that date, the date the works were handed over to the owners, stated in the same passage as 13 July 2021.

The appeal material gives two conflicting dates for the owners taking possession or handover: one passage says the owners took possession on 13 July 2017, while a later passage says the alternative handover date was 13 July 2021. The panel stated that if the contract had not specified completion, the earliest qualifying date under section 3B(3)(a) would be the date the contractor handed over possession.

The appeal panel concluded that the owners’ Tribunal application was out of time because proceedings were not commenced within seven years of completion of the building works. Section 48K(7) of the Home Building Act barred Tribunal jurisdiction over a claim for breach of a statutory warranty under Part 2C lodged more than seven years after completion, subject to the statutory alternatives if work was incomplete. The Tribunal had no power to extend the time limit, as stated with reference to S & G Homes Pty Ltd t/as Pavilion Homes v Owen [2015] NSWCATAP 190 at [53].
entities: S & G Homes Pty Ltd t/as Pavilion Homes v Owen

records.text: The appeal panel allowed Ground 6, found Ground 7 was not made out, and ordered that the appeal be allowed, the decision under appeal be set aside, and the Tribunal proceedings be dismissed. The panel also said that if its completion-date finding did not raise a question of law, it would grant leave to appeal because the Tribunal’s finding was against the weight of evidence and caused reasonably clear injustice to the builder.

The Tribunal had formed a provisional view that the builder should pay the owners’ costs and made costs orders, but the supplied excerpt ends partway through the text of order 4. The assistant’s summary says the appeal panel did not consider it appropriate to order costs against the builder.

The user is particularly interested in Yin Yoga to cultivate flexibility and inner awareness, and in how Yin Yoga and meditation can complement one another.

Beginner Yin Yoga resources suggested were YouTube classes by Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers, Dylan Werner, and Adriene, plus online classes from Paulie Zink. Practice tips included starting gently, listening to the body and avoiding pain, focusing on the breath and bodily sensations, using props, holding postures for about 3–5 minutes, practicing consistently (the assistant suggested 2–3 times weekly), being patient, and considering guidance from a qualified teacher.

The assistant described Yin Yoga as a way to prepare the body for meditation by releasing tension and encouraging relaxation and body awareness; meditation may in turn support relaxation, focus, and awareness during Yin Yoga. Suggested combining them by doing Yin Yoga before meditation, treating yoga as meditation in motion, or taking brief meditation pauses during practice.

The assistant described mindfulness as present-moment awareness practiced with curiosity and non-judgment. Suggested daily applications included mindful breathing, body scans, walking, eating, communication, ordinary tasks, and transitions between tasks; it recommended starting with short sessions, practicing consistently, and gently returning attention when the mind wanders.

The assistant suggested creamy roasted butternut squash soup made with a roughly 2-pound squash, olive oil, onion, garlic, cumin, optional smoked paprika, broth, and heavy cream or coconut cream. Roast the halved squash at 425°F (220°C) for about 45 minutes, blend the flesh, sauté onion and garlic with seasonings, then simmer with broth and cream for 15–20 minutes. records.text: On 2023-05-30, the user asked how Carvana processed vehicle titles and registrations quickly, what resources were used to optimize the process, and requested current and proposed workflows in DOT language with efficiencies highlighted. The assistant attributed faster processing to electronic title and registration systems, partnerships with state agencies, and internal processes; it outlined checking title availability, verifying buyer and seller information, and submitting forms and fees to the state agency.

On 2023-05-30, the user asked for title and registration workflow steps to address complications including vehicle liens, damaged titles, requesting titles from agencies, missing or illegible signatures, incorrect information, and incorrect dates. The assistant began by saying Carvana would verify lien information with the lending institution and ensure the lien was paid off before proceeding; the response is cut off before it explains the other issue-handling steps.

On 2023-05-30, the user clarified that they wanted a straightforward DOT-language workflow for checking lien information and validating and verifying document signatures. The assistant supplied a Graphviz DOT example with steps in this order: start, check lien information, verify document signatures, validate document information, end.
